01. Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility (DEIA) is a shared responsibility across all roles. Briefly describe how you have helped reduce barriers, promote inclusion, or support equitable outcomes in your professional practice.
LICENSES, CERTIFICATES, AND/OR OTHER REQUIREMENTS:
Construction permit procedures.
A valid California driver’s license.
A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in Planning, Civil Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, or related field.
EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE GUIDELINES
Any combination of education and experience that would likely provide the required knowledge and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain the knowledge and abilities would be:
Experience :
At least three years of increasingly responsible construction management experience, including responsibility for major capital project planning, coordination and implementation.
Education :
Applicable codes, laws rules and regulations.
Analyze problems, identify alternative solutions, project consequences of proposed actions and implement recommendations.
Budget preparation, administration and control.
Assure compliance with legal requirements and District policies.
Construction management.
Collect, compile and analyze data.
Correct English composition, grammar, spelling and vocabulary.
Develop monitor, review and manage college level construction budgets.
Design, development, construction and implementation of major capital projects.
Encourage professional excellence among the staff and promote an organizational culture of customer service, innovation, and quality
District and College policies, procedures, organization, operations and objectives.
services.
Operation of computer and office equipment.
Establish and maintain cooperative and effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.
Operation of computer, peripherals and software programs, including database management, spreadsheet, word processing and specialized software.
Interpret, apply and explain applicable federal, State, and local laws, codes and regulations.
Principles and procedures of record keeping.
Lead and facilitate group meetings effectively.
Principles of management, supervision and training.
Make informational and persuasive oral and written presentations.
Public contract administration.

State, local and federal laws, regulations, codes and requirements related to the design and construction of capital facilities projects.
Plan, organize and direct the work of consultants and contractors.

Work independently with little direction.
WORK ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The conditions herein are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions.
Work Environment:

Certain duties are performed primarily in an office environment at a desk or computer workstation. Incumbents are subject to uneven circulation paths, frequent interruptions and contact with others, in person and on the telephone. Work also requires frequent travel to various locations to attend meetings, inspect construction sites and conduct work. Must use/wear safety equipment, such as hard hat, boots, construction vest and eye protection while visiting construction sites.
Physical Demands:
The following generally describes the knowledge and ability required to enter the job and/or be learned within a short period of time in order to successfully perform the assigned duties.
Interpersonal skills including tact, patience and diplomacy.
Communicate clearly, concisely and effectively, both orally and in writing, with diverse constituencies within and outside of the District.

Commitment to equity and diversity. All applicants must have demonstrated sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students, faculty and staff. The applicant must be able to demonstrate how these factors relate to the need for equity-minded practices within an educational environment.
Oral and written communication skills, including public presentation techniques.
Operate office equipment such as computer, printer, calculator, copier and facsimile machine.
Planning and organizational skills.

Typically requires the ability to sit for long periods; use hands and fingers to operate a computer keyboard; remember key information and concentrate for prolonged periods; see to read all printed materials including, fine print and computer screen; hear and understand voices to conduct face-to-face and telephone conversations; speak in an understandable voice with sufficient volume to be heard within a normal conversational distance or on the telephone; transport self to places necessary to perform job such as meeting locations and visit and inspect construction sites; walk over uneven surfaces and through construction environments at various levels of completion, regularly bend at the waist and reach overhead, above shoulders and diagonally; lift, push, pull, move and/or carry objects weighing up to a maximum of 25 pounds.
